stories.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scores 43 points, hits go-ahead 3-pointer in Thunder's 117-112 win over Cavs
stories.summary: — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored a season-high 43 points and made a go-ahead 3-pointer with 32.6 seconds remaining as the Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 117-112 on Monday night in the first of a two-game set.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored a season-high 43 points and made a go-ahead 3-pointer with 32.6 seconds remaining as the Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 117-112 on Monday night in the first of a two-game set.


Gilgeous-Alexander attempted 35 shots, the most in the NBA during the first two weeks of the season, and made 14. He was 11 of 12 from the free-throw line in 38 minutes as the injury-depleted Thunder bounced back after two straight road losses by 20-plus points.


The fourth quarter saw eight ties and eight lead changes before Gilgeous-Alexander drilled his fourth 3-pointer. Cleveland's Sam Merrill missed a perimeter shot from the corner before Ajay Mitchell made it a two-possession game by sinking two free throws with 15.4 seconds remaining.


Oklahoma City has been reeling since the loss of three starters to long-term injuries. Mitchell scored 20 and Isaiah Hartenstein pulled down 14 rebounds.


Gilgeous-Alexander matched his highest scoring total in 17 games against the Cavaliers.


Rookie Meleek Thomas, making his first NBA start, and Donovan Mitchell led Cleveland with 17 points apiece. Mitchell also had 11 assists and Evan Mobley had 16 points.


It was the Cavaliers' first loss at home in four games this season.


The first half had 15 lead changes and two ties before the Thunder went on a 16-6 run over the last five minutes of the second quarter to take a 59-48 lead at halftime.


Gilgeous-Alexander made a pair of free throws to give Oklahoma City a 69-55 advantage with 9:26 remaining in the third. The Cavaliers battled back by going 9 of 17 from beyond the arc in the quarter.


Cleveland opened the fourth on an 18-9 run but could not sustain its momentum.


Up next
The teams meet again on Wednesday in Oklahoma City.

stories.headline: Faulk, Brandsegg-Nygård score early in 3rd, lift Red Wings past Panthers 5-3
stories.summary: — Justin Faulk and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård scored 45 seconds apart early in the third period, goalie Daniil Tarasov defeated his former team and the surging Detroit Red Wings beat the Florida Panthers 5-3 on Monday night.
stories.body:
SUNRISE, Fla. -- — Justin Faulk and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård scored 45 seconds apart early in the third period, goalie Daniil Tarasov defeated his former team and the surging Detroit Red Wings beat the Florida Panthers 5-3 on Monday night.


Faulk had a power-play tally to put Detroit up 3-2 at 2:08 of the third, and Brandsegg-Nygård lifted one over the glove of Florida goalie Jacob Markstrom from deep in the slot to give the Red Wings a two-goal edge.


Carter Mazur got his first NHL goal for Detroit to open the scoring, Alex DeBrincat got his seventh of the season for the Red Wings and Emmitt Finnie sealed it on an empty-netter for three seconds left. Tarasov, who spent last season backing up Sergei Bobrovsky with the Panthers, stopped 23 shots for Detroit.


Aaron Ekblad scored his first goal of the season — and the third short-handed goal of his 13-year career — for Florida, while Sam Reinhart scored his eighth of the year for the Panthers. Markstrom made 24 saves in his first game since Oct. 17.


Florida saw its three-game winning streak snapped. The Panthers never led, with Mazur's goal putting the Wings up 1-0 and DeBrincat making it 2-1 after early in the second after Reinhart tied the game with 5:41 left in the opening period.


Sam Bennett got his fourth of the year for Florida, with Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk assisting in a 6-on-5 opportunity with 3:21 left.


Detroit is now 6-2-1 in its last nine games yet still remains tied for the fewest points in the jampacked Atlantic Division, which had eight teams separated by six points entering Monday. It is, by far, the closest division right now in the NHL; the other three entered Monday's games with an average gap of 15.7 points between first place and last place.


Up next
Red Wings: At Tampa Bay on Tuesday night.


Panthers: Hosts Chicago on Wednesday night.

stories.headline: Ravens QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) has chance to play Thursday, per Jesse Minter
stories.summary: Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury but has "a chance" to play Thursday night, coach Jesse Minter said.
stories.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- With the Baltimore Ravens' top three quarterbacks dealing with injuries, coach Jesse Minter was not definitive on who will be his starter for Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

In addition to Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) being ruled out for Thursday's game, the Ravens' No. 3 quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury.

"To Joe's credit, he's kind of fighting through a couple things he's dealing with," Minter said after Monday night's walk-through, "but expect him to have a chance to play on Thursday."

Fagnano was listed as a limited participant in Monday's walk-through practice.

Fagnano would become just the second undrafted rookie quarterback to start in the Ravens' 32-year history. The first undrafted rookie quarterback to start for Baltimore was Anthony Brown during the Ravens' 27-16 loss in the 2022 season finale at the Cincinnati Bengals.

The only healthy quarterback on the roster is Austin Reed, who was signed to the practice squad Monday. Reed, 26, has familiarity with the offensive system because he spent time at Ravens training camp this summer and also played under offensive coordinator Declan Doyle when they were both in Chicago last year.

Asked if the Ravens' quarterback situation is up in the air, Minter replied, "I think we'll figure that out over the next day or two."

Minter indicated that Baltimore could have a more definitive timetable on Jackson sometime this week. After Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo, Minter said Jackson's injury "potentially" could be season-ending. Jackson, who will go on injured reserve, has not had surgery on his right thumb yet, according to Minter.

"I think when you lose a guy like Lamar, it's a little bit of every phase doing a little bit more," Minter said. "So, it's being able to play really good defense, being able to maybe make a play or steal a play on special teams, maybe a different style of offense of how we need to play."

Huntley, the Ravens' primary backup quarterback, will not play Thursday night, according to Minter. "We'll see how it goes from a long-term standpoint," Minter said.

The Ravens (4-4), who have lost three straight to fall into last place in the AFC North, are set to make a change at kicker. Minter said kicker Tyler Loop "potentially" might go on injured reserve because of a right groin injury.

"I would say [Loop was] dealing with something small that it kind of became a little bit more and leave it at that," Minter said.

Loop was listed as a nonparticipant in Monday's walk-through.

In his second season, Loop has struggled with consistency. He is 2-of-6 inside 50 yards, missing a 34-yard field goal attempt Sunday.

The Ravens have Jake Moody, a third-round pick in 2023 by the San Francisco 49ers, on the practice squad. Asked if Moody will kick Thursday, Minter said, "At this point, yes."

The Ravens are 8.5-point underdogs to the Jaguars, according to DraftKings. This marks their largest underdog role at home since December 2021, when they were 9-point underdogs to the Green Bay Packers.

stories.headline: Moyes after 2nd Everton win over Newcastle: 'Not an easy thing'
stories.summary: David Moyes hailed a "great result" for Everton as they secured back-to-back wins over Newcastle United with a 1-0 triumph at St James' Park on Monday.
stories.body:
David Moyes hailed a "great result" for Everton as they secured back-to-back wins over Newcastle United with a 1-0 triumph at St James' Park on Monday, calling it no easy feat.

Monday night's Premier League clash took place just four days after the Toffees claimed a 3-1 victory over the Magpies in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and Moyes' side were able to secure three points on Tyneside.

A first half lacking in clear-cut chances from both sides saw Everton take the lead just four minutes after the restart when Tyrique George's low effort squeezed underneath Lukás Hornícek.

Thierno Barry then reacted quickly to pounce on the loose ball and stab home for his fourth league goal of the campaign.

Moyes said recording successive wins over the Magpies in such a short space of time was "not an easy thing," but was full of praise for his side's display as they claimed three points.

"They are so good in what they do as they give everything they've got," the Everton boss said.

"They're a brilliant group of players and they've had it tough as well. They want to keep winning and they've found it difficult with the way things have gone, but they're pulling it out and doing their best to be in all the games.

"It's never easy ... we beat Newcastle on Thursday night and to beat them again today is not an easy thing to do for any club and this level.

"To come here and get a good win tonight was a great result for us."

Victory ends a three-game winless run for Everton in the Premier League and sees them move into seventh in the standings, but Moyes was also pleased to earn a first away win in their league campaign.

He added: "We've actually done quite well in some of the games getting draws in difficult away games, but we've not picked up a victory and last season we had a great run of results away from home.

"So I was hoping to pick it up tonight and thankfully we did, clean sheet and got the goal that counted."

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle admitted his side need to "do things better" following a disappointing performance.

The Magpies struggled to threaten throughout the match and were frustrated further when Jacob Ramsey was dismissed with two yellow cards in quick succession at the death to leave the Tynesiders 13th in the table.

Asked what the solution is, Jaissle said: "We need to analyse that now in detail.

"It's also clear that I have the responsibility and I also take that as the manager of this club, and we need to do things better.

"There were many things there, not only in possession, which was not on the level we expected to see.

"Also out of possession, we wanted to press them high, we wanted to stretch them as soon as possible and make also a clear distinction if that was overplayed from their position that we defend in a compact block, but nothing between.

"Again, it was not much seen today on the pitch."

stories.headline: Valkyries, Lynx, Aces all seen as WNBA title favorites
stories.summary: The defending champion Valkyries are seen as favorites to win next year's WNBA title at one sportsbook, while the Lynx and Aces are favorites at others.
stories.body:
After coming into 2026 as 45-1 underdogs to win the WNBA Finals, the Golden State Valkyries captured their first title in just their second season in existence. Golden State's odds to do it again next season are much shorter, but sportsbooks around the country have not come to a consensus on who should be favored for the championship.

The Valkyries are the favorites to win the 2027 WNBA Finals at BetMGM, showing +300 odds, but at DraftKings, the Minnesota Lynx -- who notched the 2026 regular season's best record -- are the favorites at +310, while Caesars Sportsbook and FanDuel have the Las Vegas Aces favored at +340 and +360, respectively. The 2026 runner-up Atlanta Dream are within the top four at each of those sportsbooks, showing a short number of +400 at DraftKings.

Bookmakers have different rationales for where they placed each team on the Finals odds board. DraftKings director of sports operations Johnny Avello favored the Lynx despite their unceremonious end to the 2026 season and some offseason uncertainty.

"Minnesota's power rating is slightly above Las Vegas, Atlanta & Golden State," he told ESPN by email. "The pairing of last year's Rookie of the Year, Olivia Miles, and Napheesa Collier is lethal, as they are two MVP type players. Only concern is that Collier is a free agent, and could sign elsewhere. Atlanta is also marginally ahead of Golden State as they strengthen the team by getting Brionna Jones back, who played just nine games this past season."

Caesars Sportsbook's lead pro basketball oddsmaker, David Lieberman, noted that his book's power ratings are mostly the same from the end of the season and that "the championship odds mostly reflect the potential ceiling of each team" taking into account how things could shake out in the offseason.

Just outside the top tier are Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever (+900 at DraftKings) and Paige Bueckers' Dallas Wings, who are a relatively long 14-1 at DraftKings but as short as +750 at BetMGM. There's also a wide range of odds on the New York Liberty, who are anywhere between +900 and 17-1 for the 2027 title after a relatively disappointing 2026 campaign that saw them come in as favorites.

Indiana has perennially been one of the most popular futures plays by public bettors since Clark joined the league, but Dallas has been encroaching on that territory since Bueckers' debut. Both teams bowed out of the 2026 playoffs in the first round, and bookmakers aren't putting too much stock into their championship aspirations just yet especially given other teams' talent and some potential roster changes.

"The Fever need to re-sign Kelsey Mitchell, or their odds will go even higher," Avello said. "We're not worried about the general public piling on them to win it all -- their liability wasn't as high as the prior two seasons. New stars continue to emerge in the league, which does take some of the attention off Clark."

The Wings, meanwhile, "are a young and exciting team, but it remains to be seen if they'll be able to play enough defense to truly compete for a title just yet, similar to the questions surrounding the Fever," Lieberman said. "I expect to see quite a lot of action on both teams throughout the offseason in the futures markets."

Avello also said DraftKings is wary of the Washington Mystics, who were a surprising playoff team this season after coming into the 2026 campaign with 150-1 championship odds. Washington's young core has them at 35-1 for the 2027 title at DraftKings and as short as 11-1 at BetMGM.

For all of the potential contenders atop the board, there is also a cadre of long shots at the bottom, with the Chicago Sky, Seattle Storm, Toronto Tempo and relocating Houston Comets coming in at 120-1, per DraftKings lines.

stories.headline: George Russell admits his F1 season had 'more bad days than good' following Kimi Antonelli championship triumph
stories.summary: George Russell has admitted his 2026 Formula 1 season has been the first of his career with "more bad days than good" in a candid first statement following Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli's world championship triumph.
stories.body:
George Russell has admitted his 2026 Formula 1 season has been the first of his career with "more bad days than good" in a candid first statement following Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli's world championship triumph.

Russell skipped media duties after Antonelli became F1's youngest world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, with team boss Toto Wolff admittIng his driver was "distraught" and suffering a "catastrophic moment".

The Englishman had entered the season as a strong favourite and won the opening race of the year but never recovered from five straight Antonelli victories which followed.

Russell congratulated Antonelli when he got out of the car after Sunday's race and did so again in a social media post on Monday, in which he vowed to rediscover his old form.

"Now feels like a pretty suitable moment to speak from the heart," Russell said.

"This season started off exactly how I had hoped but it very quickly unravelled with tough luck and poor performances. It's been the first proper season of my career where I've had more bad days than good.

"All I know is that I've given it my all and 2026 was not meant to be my year. I want to sincerely congratulate Kimi on what has been an absolutely incredible season. You truly deserve the Championship.

"Thank you to the team for producing the best car and power unit this season; it's been inspiring to see everyone coming together over four tough years to bring Mercedes back to the top.

"Now, all I can promise is that for the rest of this season, and into the next one, I will be giving my absolute all to rediscover the performance I have been capable of producing for the majority of my career and fingers crossed a little bit of luck returns."

The families that built Kimi Antonelli, F1 world champion

- In pictures: The moments that defined Kimi Antonelli's F1 title-winning season
Russell joined Mercedes in 2022, on the back of eight consecutive constructors' championships for the team.

However, his arrival coincided with a rule change and a downturn in fortunes, and the team only won a handful of races until this season. Mercedes entered F1's new era, with engines featuring a near 50-50 split between conventional combustion power and electrical components, as the benchmark team to beat.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

Dreyer -- a back-to-back MLS All-Star -- won't feature in this year's postseason, but that didn't stop him from handing the recently-crowded U.S. Open Cup champions a loss in a 1-0 victory over St. Louis. Dreyer's left-footed chip from distance was a taste of quality we'll be missing seven days from now.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 24

With no postseason hopes, victories must come from small achievements, like letting Reus assist three goals or having a goalkeeper make six saves while still conceding four.

26. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

Toronto succumbed to a 3-1 defeat to Atlanta and ended their postseason dream in the process. Back to the drawing board for Robin Fraser's side, who showed signs of potential earlier in the season.

27. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 28

With the playoffs out of the picture and the all-time goals conceded in a single season record newly secured, SKC still did their best to sabotage Dallas by absconding with a 1-1 draw against a side looking to lock up their top-two finish in the Western Conference.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Miguel Almirón won't appear in this year's playoffs, so he put on an end-of-season show in a 3-1 win against Toronto while eliminating the fellow Eastern Conference team from the playoffs. Five Stripes fans will take what they can get this year.

29. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

After losing to Toronto in the midweek, D.C. played Columbus with the playoffs already out of the picture and proceeded to lose 3-0. With 11 years since their last postseason victory, there's nowhere to go but up for this MLS original.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

It's too late to save their season, but not too late to sink somebody else's. A 91st-minute response to NYCFC's 1-0 lead secured their 26th point of the year and put to rest New York's postseason dream.

stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: Harry Grant calls for shorter NRL season amid contract chaos, Cup blowouts
stories.summary: Kangaroos hooker Harry Grant has called for the NRL to shorten the regular season in a bid to avoid the contracting circus which has engulfed Australia's Rugby League World Cup campaign.
stories.body:
Kangaroos hooker Harry Grant has called for the NRL to shorten the regular season in a bid to avoid the contracting circus which has engulfed Australia's Rugby League World Cup campaign.

In a move which Grant believes would also strengthen the international game, the Melbourne captain claims a shorter season would allow players to focus on Test commitments before resolving their futures.

Close to half of the squad selected by Kevin Walters entered the final 12 months of their deals on November 1.

"Maybe we could shorten the season, then you have a World Cup where everyone can play footy and you have your conversations off the back of that," Grant said.

"That's an easy idea, and I know there's an understanding that maybe a shorter season would get a bit more footy and open up some rep windows with Origin, Australia, Samoa, and Tonga."

With the Perth Bears entering the competition in 2027 and the PNG Chiefs joining 12 months later, existing NRL clubs are urgently looking to get surety on their rosters for the seasons ahead.

The Sydney Roosters withdrawing their offer of an extension to premiership-winning halfback Sam Walker in the aftermath of his Australia Test debut is perhaps the best example.

The flow-on effect of the Roosters' shock stance led to speculation that Canberra five-eighth Ethan Strange and North Queensland halfback Tom Dearden - both of whom are in Australian camp with Walker - are now linked with moves to Easts.

"I'd like to think we can have some mature conversations collectively going forward. I've certainly got some opinions myself, but it doesn't mean they're always right.

"If you get a few things that you think can take the game forward in a better fashion, then I'm all for it."

Grant is also of the belief that a shorter season would allow the sport's powerbrokers to generate a more meaningful international calendar which helped strengthen smaller Test nations.

The hooker has seen France and the Cook Islands - the only two sides to not win a game at this World Cup - be lambs to the slaughter against opposing teams stacked with NRL players.

But Grant sees value in giving those teams more exposure to playing elite opposition outside of World Cups.

"With this World Cup, you see that there's a real market for the games and whether there is a window at the end of the year it's also about giving those guys opportunities," Grant said.

"I don't know how many games France or the Cook Islands get to play together since the last World Cup (in 2022).

"There's certainly an opportunity for those teams, even New Zealand, Tonga, and Samoa, to get together and have more games.

"I look at France, and since the World Cup last time, how many games have they played together? I think there might be an opportunity to allow those teams to play more footy together."

stories.headline: Barry leads Everton to second win over Newcastle in four days
stories.summary: Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle at St James' Park.
stories.body:
Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle United at St James' Park.

Following a first half lacking in clear-cut opportunities, the Toffees took the lead shortly after the restart when Barry stabbed home his fourth league goal of the campaign.

A frustrating night soured further for the Magpies as they finished the game with 10 men when substitute Jacob Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession at the death.

Everton ended a three-game winless run in the Premier League and moved up to seventh in the table, while Newcastle slipped to 13th.

Monday's match took place just four days after Everton's 3-1 win over Newcastle in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and both sides made two changes to their starting XI as Anthony Elanga and Joelinton came in for the Magpies, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Harrison Armstrong lined up for the visitors.

Harvey Barnes looked lively on the left flank for the hosts, sending a curling shot wide before his looping cross floated narrowly past the far post and Jordan Pickford was forced to hold Will Osula's deflected cross from a tight angle.

Joelinton had an effort blocked by James Tarkowski and Merlin Röhl fired over the crossbar as both sides looked to break the deadlock.

James Garner blasted a free kick from the edge of the area straight into the Newcastle wall and Barnes was at the heart of the action again, firing in a dangerous cross which bounced off Branthwaite and was tipped over by Pickford.

Joelinton unleashed a fierce strike from distance which whizzed wide and Everton enjoyed a late flurry of chances before the break.

Jake O'Brien was unable to nod home Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's cross and Harrison Armstrong skewed a first-time effort wide.

The Toffees picked up where they left off only four minutes into the second half when a slick pass from a free kick set Tyrique George free on the left to fire low at Lukás Hornícek.

His shot squeezed underneath the Newcastle goalkeeper, but Barry was quick to react to tap in the loose ball and the goal stood following a VAR check for two close offside calls.

Branthwaite's header was tipped away by Hornicek as the visitors looked to quickly double their advantage, while Fabian Schär hooked an effort over the crossbar and Pickford held Joe Willock's header.

Hornicek was then called into action at the opposite end to push away Dewsbury-Hall's strike and the Magpies goalkeeper made a solid low save from the resulting corner to deny O'Brien.

Barnes' cross from the left was nearly turned in by Elanga at the far post, but the ball hit the post and trickled across the goal-line before being cleared.

Newcastle looked to threaten around the Everton box as Pickford punched away Jacob Murphy's corner and the ball was recycled back to Ramsey, who dragged his volley narrowly wide.

Yoane Wissa's shot was comfortably held by Pickford, who made another solid stop from the striker in the 90th minute with his feet.

With eight minutes added on, the home side were frustrated further when Ramsey was dismissed after picking up two yellow cards within minutes of each other as they slipped to defeat.

stories.headline: Astros owner Jim Crane hails Randy Flores as a 'perfect fit' as team's GM
stories.summary: Randy Flores was introduced as the 15th general manager of the Astros on Monday.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- The Astros interviewed a variety of candidates in the search for their next general manager.

It quickly became clear that Randy Flores was their guy.

"We went over it and over it and over it and as we reflected back on everybody we spoke to and the qualities, we were looking for Randy was a perfect fit," Astros owner Jim Crane said Monday. "He has experience in every single area of baseball, and you don't find that very often and he has been trained and been around some good organizations. So, he stood out at the end."

Flores was introduced as the 15th general manager of the Astros on Monday after being hired on Friday to replace Dana Brown, who was let go in August with his contract set to expire at the end of the season.

The Astros cut ties with Brown on Aug. 24. Three assistant general managers and Hall of Famer and special adviser Jeff Bagwell took over his responsibilities for the remainder of the season while Crane sought a replacement.

Flores had been serving as the St. Louis Cardinals' assistant general manager of amateur and pro acquisition.

The former major league pitcher joined the Cardinals' front office as director of scouting in 2015 and spent eight seasons (2019-26) as an assistant GM with the club.

He said there is a mixture of excitement and nerves as well as another emotion as he embarks on his first general manager job.

"There's a weight to the role," he said. "Does that make sense? A weight and a responsibility. That's what I feel right now, actually."

His first order of business will be hiring a manager after Joe Espada's contract was not renewed after the AL West Champions were swept by the Chicago White Sox in their Wild Card Series.

Flores said he'll get to work on that task immediately and shared some things he'll be looking for when filling that position.

"The qualities you look for, in coordination with Jim, we're talking about trust, we're talking about energy, we're talking about chemistry," he said.

Crane added that he interviewed a few managerial candidates before hiring Flores.

"But now that we've got Randy in place, he'll take over that process along with our team and we'll get to work on that," he said. "We hope to get that filled very quickly."

After that they'll set their sights on working on the roster for next season. And Crane said he doesn't envision it being a rebuilding year.

"I don't think it's going to be a complete tear down at all," he said. "I think we've got enough talent to work with, and we've got to make some good decisions and make some changes and solidify a better lineup and a better team than we had last year."

He pointed out that even though the season had a disappointing ending, Houston did return to the postseason after missing out the previous year. The Astros went 81-81 to win the AL West for the fifth time in six years, becoming the first big league club without a winning record to reach the playoffs in a non-shortened season.

"We did make the playoffs, which is always the goal," Crane said. "But we have very high standards here and so I'm sure these guys will get together and make some good decisions, and you'll see some changes made with the roster, surely."

Flores pitched in the majors for eight seasons from 2002-10, going 11-5 with a 4.61 ERA and four saves. The left-hander made 347 relief appearances and three starts for Texas, Colorado, St. Louis and Minnesota.

Crane likes that Flores played professionally, a quality that very few MLB general managers have. Additionally, Crane, who made his fortune as a shipping magnate, was impressed with all of the different roles Flores has served in the Cardinals front office.

"His resume is so complete that you very rarely find a guy that's worked in every single department," Crane said. "I started on the dock in my business and made it to the top. So, I think it's very important to know how everything functions and what those people are doing and how they're doing it and determine if they're doing it well or not doing it well."

Flores said the quality from his playing days that he thinks will help him succeed in his new role is his competitiveness.

"I'm competitive," he said. "We're all competitive in this game. Otherwise, why do this job ... we want development, we want process, but ultimately every night there's a real game. It's not expected outcomes. It's not probabilities. It's a win and a loss, and there's 162 of them, and I can't wait to be in that fight with this team."

stories.headline: Where do 2026 champion Valkyries rank among every WNBA title team?
stories.summary: Las Vegas' 2023 title team topped our rankings two years ago. Where do the 2026 Valkyries fit in?
stories.body:
On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA title in just their second year to put the finishing touches on the league's 30th season. Where do they rank among all of the WNBA champions?

The Valkyries built their reputation on being a complete team that relied on defense. At 67.4 points per game, they had the lowest scoring average in the Finals of any champion since Sacramento (66.8 PPG) in 2005. Golden State is also one of just five WNBA champions that averaged fewer points in the WNBA Finals than the team it defeated for the title.

But the Valkyries lit up the Bay Area Halloween celebrations with their thrilling second-half comeback victory in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals. The league went to a best-of-seven format for the Finals in 2025, but this year was the first to go the distance. The No. 2 seed Valkyries won three times at home at Chase Center in the series and once on the road at State Farm Arena.

Gabby Williams, in her first year with Golden State, was the Valkyries' go-to player who performed offensively at a superstar level in the postseason. She averaged 21.0 points in 13 playoff games, including five of 25 points or more. Her 30 points in Game 7 helped secure the WNBA Finals MVP award. In those seven games, she averaged 19.6 points, which ranks 19th among the 30 Finals MVPs.

The Valkyries did it their way: 100% committed to defense and a process that worked all season. And even though they don't rank in the top 10 all time, being anywhere on this list is great because these teams are all the ultimate winners.

1. 2023 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 34-6, 8-1

Defeated the New York Liberty 3-1 in Finals

As good as they were in winning the 2022 championship, the Aces were even better in 2023. They ranked No. 1 in scoring and defense during the Regular-season and stumbled just once in the playoffs, in Game 3 of the Finals. A'ja Wilson got her first WNBA Finals MVP honor for her performance in 2023; she won again for the 2025 Finals.

In Chelsea Gray, Kelsey Plum and Jackie Young, the Aces also had trio of guards who were among the best backcourts in league history.

Candace Parker, a free agent signee who was expected to be a big part of the Aces' 2023 title run, was sidelined by foot surgery that July. The Aces also lost starters Gray and Kiah Stokes before Game 4 and still won the title, illustrating how good the chemistry was for the team. The Las Vegas bench -- then led by Alysha Clark, Cayla George, Sydney Colson and Kierstan Bell -- came through when they were needed most.

2. 2000 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-5, 6-0

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-0 in Finals

This was the last of Houston's four consecutive title teams, the end of the Comets' version of "Camelot." In 2000, the WNBA was at 16 teams and most of the former ABL players were in their second year in the league. Sheryl Swoopes won her first of three MVP awards and two-time MVP Cynthia Cooper played her last full season at age 37.

As was the case with the other Houston championship teams, the stars carried them: Swoopes and Cooper averaged 35 minutes a game, Tina Thompson 34 and Janeth Arcain 30.5. Fifth starter, Tiffani Johnson (22.2), was the only other player who averaged at least 20 minutes a game. With three future Hall of Famers (Cooper, Swoopes, Thompson), Houston didn't need much statistically from its reserves. The Comets' bench players knew their roles, and the team knew how to win. This title ended the dynasty -- the Los Angeles Sparks were ascending -- but what a finish.

3. 2020 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 18-4, 6-0

Defeated the Las Vegas Aces 3-0 in Finals

Point guard Sue Bird, part of all four Storm title teams, has ruminated over which of them was "best." Lauren Jackson was the superstar of the 2004 and 2010 Storm title teams; her counterpart in 2018 and 2020 was Breanna Stewart. Bird said an edge goes to the very similarly constructed 2018 and 2020 teams due to the presence of guard Jewell Loyd. Bird then gives a nod to the overall depth and chemistry to the 2020 Storm, who were first in the league in offensive and defensive rating.

"The way we shot 3's, the way we moved the ball -- if you took something away, we'd just keep it moving," Bird said. "We talked before every game that we were going to wear teams out with the pace that we played."

4. 2013 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 7-0

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

This was the second of four Lynx titles in a seven-season span. They didn't have the best regular-season record among Lynx champs; both 2011 and 2017 went 27-7 (and the 2016 runners-up were 28-6). But coach Cheryl Reeve said the "core four" of the franchise -- Seimone Augustus, Rebekkah Brunson, Maya Moore and Lindsay Whalen -- were near the peak of their collective powers in 2013. They all averaged double figures in scoring, led by Moore's 18.5 PPG. The fifth starter was Janel McCarville, Whalen's former University of Minnesota teammate, and that pairing again thrilled Gophers fans.

In 2012, Minnesota lost 3-1 in the Finals to Indiana, which irked the Lynx because they were five games better than the Fever in the regular-season standings. The 2013 team didn't allow any openings in the playoffs, sweeping Seattle, Phoenix and Atlanta.

5. 1998 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-3, 4-1

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 2-1 in Finals

Cooper said if she had to pick just one Comets championship team as her favorite, it would be this one. The team's .900 winning percentage (27-3) remains the best in WNBA history. Swoopes was second on the team in scoring at 15.6 PPG to Cooper's 22.7. Cooper won her second consecutive MVP award; she was Finals MVP for all four championship teams.

And there's another reason this team is dear to Cooper's heart. Her close friend, Kim Perrot, the Comets' spark plug point guard, averaged 8.5 points and 4.7 assists in what would be her last season in the WNBA. Perrot had 13 points, five rebounds and four assists in the title-clinching win over the Mercury. Five months later, she was diagnosed with cancer and died in August 1999 at age 32.

6. 2014 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 29-5, 7-1

Defeated the Chicago Sky 3-0 in Finals

Amid the Lynx dynasty from 2011 to 2017, the Mercury owned this season. Their 29 wins was a WNBA record at that time, and they were first in offensive and defensive rating. All five starters -- Diana Taurasi, Brittney Griner, Candice Dupree, Penny Taylor and DeWanna Bonner -- averaged double digits in scoring.

Their only loss in the playoffs came to Minnesota in Game 2 of the Western Conference finals, but they bounced back to win the series with an 18-point Game 3 victory. In the WNBA Finals, Chicago was no match. Taurasi, who averaged 16.2 PPG in the Regular-season and 21.9 PPG in the playoffs, was WNBA Finals MVP for the second time.

7. 2017 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-7, 6-2

Defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 3-2 in Finals

Minnesota was still smarting over a 3-2 Finals loss to Los Angeles in 2016, and the teams were again archrivals in 2017. Minnesota was first in the league in offensive and defensive rating and Los Angeles was second in both.

Target Center was being renovated, so the Lynx's home games in the 2017 playoffs were at the University of Minnesota' Williams Arena, where Whalen had played in college. The decisive 85-76 Game 5 win came in a packed and cacophonous Williams, and Fowles was Finals MVP for a second time (she also won in 2015).

8. 2019 Washington Mystics

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-3

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-2 in Finals

Elena Delle Donne said this was the best team she has ever played on: "Not just talent-wise, but the way emotionally and mentally we were so on-point with one another. That's what took us to the next level."

The Mystics were more dominant in the Regular-season than the playoffs, but had to overcome a back injury that hampered Delle Donne during the Finals. She was the MVP in 2019, but teammate Emma Meesseman was the Finals MVP, averaging 17.8 points in the championship series.

9. 2022 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 26-10, 8-2

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-1 in Finals

The 2022 Aces ran into more challenges in the Regular-season than the 2023 version of Las Vegas. But by the playoffs, they were in control as the league's best team.

In coach Becky Hammon's first season with the franchise, the Aces changed their playing style -- 3-pointers became a far bigger part of the offense -- and Plum and Young matured into even better players. Wilson won her second regular-season MVP award and was Defensive Player of the Year. Then Gray was on fire throughout the playoffs, winning Finals MVP.

It was a big achievement for a franchise that started when the league did in 1997, in Utah, moved to San Antonio, and then found its championship home in Las Vegas under owner Mark Davis. He paid top dollar to bring Hammon from the NBA, where she was a San Antonio Spurs assistant, and it was a great investment.

10. 1999 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-6, 4-2

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-1 in Finals

In 1999, almost all the former ABL standouts had transitioned into and strengthened the WNBA. That didn't stop the Comets, who added former ABL player Sonja Henning at point guard. Houston's standouts were the same as in 1998: Cooper, Swoopes and Thompson. Bulgarian center Polina Tzekova, then 31, made the most of her only WNBA season, starting every game for Houston in 1999.

Ultimately, there was a melancholy feel to the 1999 championship for the Comets. Their former point guard Perrot died from cancer on Aug. 19. After being stunned by Liberty guard Teresa Weatherspoon's buzzer-beating halfcourt heave in Game 2 of the Finals, Houston won Game 3 and secured its third title in honor of Perrot.

11. 2024 New York Liberty
Regular-season and playoff records: 32-8, 8-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-2 in Finals

It took 27 years since the launch of the Liberty as an original WNBA franchise in 1997, but New York finally broke through for its first championship. After finishing with the best record in the league, the Liberty defeated defending champion Las Vegas in the semifinals and then avenged a Commissioner's Cup final loss to Minnesota in the Finals.

The deciding Game 5 vs. the Lynx nearly extended the Liberty's long postseason heartbreak. But a late foul (still disputed by Minnesota) sent Breanna Stewart to the line. She scored the tying points to send the game into overtime, where New York prevailed 67-62.

Jonquel Jones won the Finals MVP honor as she got her first title. Sabrina Ionescu also won the championship for the first time. It was the third title for Stewart, who won two championships in Seattle.

12. 2001 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 28-4, 6-1

Defeated the Charlotte Sting 2-0 in Finals

The Sparks learned a lot going against Houston for four seasons before making their championship breakthrough. Los Angeles star Lisa Leslie has joked, "Thank God that Coop retired," in reference to the Houston's Cooper ending her playing career after the 2000 season (she returned for four games in 2003 at age 40).

Leslie, Mwadi Mabika, Tamecka Dixon and DeLisha Milton-Jones all averaged in double figures during this title run. Leslie was MVP for the season and the Finals.

13. 2011 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 27-7, 7-1

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

In 2010, Minnesota got a new coach (Reeve) and also added Whalen (trade) and Brunson (Sacramento dispersal draft). The next year brought the opening championship of the Lynx dynasty as No. 1 pick Moore was Rookie of the Year. The 22-year-old Moore started alongside Taj McWilliams-Franklin, who turned 41 two weeks after the Finals ended. This Lynx team really spanned the age/experience gamut.

The season also brought a well-deserved spotlight to Augustus, who became the original building block for the dynasty when she was drafted No. 1 in 2006. She led the 2011 Lynx in scoring in the Regular-season (16.2) and playoffs (22.0) and was the Finals MVP.

14. 2016 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-2 in Finals

After winning back-to-back titles in 2001-02, the Sparks endured a lot of frustrating "almost" in the playoffs. They lost in the WNBA Finals in 2003 and the conference finals in 2006, 2008, 2009 and 2012. The playoff format changed in 2016, seeding the top eight teams regardless of conference, and the Sparks made the Finals again. In an epic five-game series, they beat Minnesota 77-76 on Nneka Ogwumike's putback with 3.1 seconds remaining. Ogwumike was the season MVP and teammate Candace Parker the Finals MVP. It was the last jewel to complete Parker's crown; she already had won two NCAA titles and two Olympic gold medals.

15. 2025 Las Vegas Aces
Regular-season and playoff records: 30-14, 9-3

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 4-0 in Finals

The 2025 Aces might be the most difficult champion to rank because the first half of their five-month season (counting playoffs) was so different from the second half. But some key factors elevate them to the middle of the pack in the rankings.

The first is the play of Wilson, who won her fourth regular-season MVP and second Finals MVP. During the playoffs, she averaged 26.8 PPG, 10.0 RPG, 3.3 assists and 2.5 blocks. Her postseason performance was even greater than in the Regular-season. She also hit the most crucial shot of the Finals: the game winner with less than a second left in Game 3 to give the Aces a 90-88 victory.

The Aces also got a terrific postseason from guards Jackie Young (20.4 PPG, 5.5 APG) and Chelsea Gray (11.2 PPG, 7.3 APG).

The Aces' 17-game winning streak (counting Game 1 of the playoffs) is the second longest in WNBA history. And coach Becky Hammon led the Aces to a third championship in four years despite having to replace a key player (guard Kelsey Plum) from the first two title teams. The Aces are the league's ultimate example that it's not how you start, it's how you finish.

16. 2018 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 26-8, 6-2

Defeated the Washington Mystics 3-0 in Finals

History repeated itself with the Storm. They had back-to-back No. 1 picks in Jackson and Bird in 2001 and 2002, which led to two titles. Seattle again got consecutive No. 1s in 2015 and 2016 with Loyd and Stewart, which also led to two titles. This 2018 championship in a lot of ways was won in the semifinals, when the Storm held off Phoenix in an epic Game 5 in which Bird took over in the fourth quarter. In the finals, Seattle wasn't going to be denied and swept the Mystics. And the Storm looked to be a strong threat to become the first repeat champion since the Sparks in 2001-02. But an Achilles injury kept Stewart out in 2019. When she returned in 2020, the Storm picked up where they had left off in 2018.

17. 2010 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 28-6, 7-0

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 3-0 in Finals

The 2010 Storm were six games better than any team in the WNBA; no other team in the Western Conference even had a winning record. Jackson won her third MVP award, and she and Bird got to celebrate their second WNBA championship together. Bird, Swin Cash and Svetlana Abrosimova, who had won an NCAA title together at UConn in 2000, all played for this Storm team. Seattle didn't lose at home in 2010, which ended up being Jackson's last full season in the WNBA, as injuries forced her out of the league after 2012.

18. 2005 Sacramento Monarchs

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-9, 7-1

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 3-1 in Finals

After losing in the conference finals three of the previous four years, the Monarchs won in 2005.

At age 29, Yolanda Griffith entered the WNBA in 1999 from the ABL and was her new league's MVP that year, a perfect target for point guard Ticha Penicheiro.

Griffith also won Finals MVP, and it was a career-best year for DeMya Walker, who led the Monarchs in scoring in the Regular-season and made an All-Star appearance. This was also the first of Rebekkah Brunson's five WNBA titles; her other four came with Minnesota.

19. 2002 Los Angeles Sparks

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-7, 6-0

Defeated the New York Liberty 2-0 in Finals

The Sparks' repeat championship seemed more predictable than extraordinary at the time, coming after Houston had won four in a row. But it took two decades for another franchise to go back-to-back, with the Aces doing it in 2022-2023. That makes Los Angeles' achievement stand out more now. There isn't much to separate this Sparks team from the 2001 Sparks, who had a little better regular-season record (28-4 in 2001 to 25-7 in 2002). The standout players were the same except for Nikki Teasley, a rookie in 2002 who hit the championship-clinching 3-pointer in Game 2 of the Finals.

20. 2026 Golden State Valkyries

Regular-season and playoff records: 32-12, 9-4

Defeated the Atlanta Dream 4-3 in Finals

Much has been made of the Valkyries being the first champions without any All-WNBA selections in the season they won the title. They also are the first team since the 2013 Minnesota Lynx to not have a current or former season MVP on the roster at the time of their championship.

This largely reflects the Valkyries' focus on defense: The All-WNBA first and second teams are generally tilted toward big offensive stats. So a lot of credit must go to Golden State's team chemistry and an outstanding coaching job by Natalie Nakase and her staff.

In the playoffs, the Valkyries beat teams with some of the top offensive players in the league: Dallas' Paige Bueckers and Arike Ogunbowale, Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray, and Atlanta's Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray.

As mentioned, the Valkyries are one of five WNBA champions who averaged fewer points in the Finals than their opponent (67.4 PPG to Atlanta's 71.4); the others are Las Vegas (2022), Los Angeles (2016), and Detroit twice (2006, 2003). But the Dream's Finals scoring average was still 20 points lower than their regular-season average, plus Golden State held Atlanta under 65 points in all four of its victories.

It was very impressive, and as time passes, the Valkyries' performance might move up even more in historical regard.

21. 2006 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-3

Defeated the Sacramento Monarchs 3-2 in Finals

A big key for this team was the 2005 midseason trade that brought Katie Smith to the Shock. She fit in well with Cash, Cheryl Ford, Deanna Nolan and Ruth Riley, who were all on Detroit's 2003 championship squad.

Nolan, a native of nearby Flint, Michigan, was Finals MVP as the Shock prevented Sacramento's attempt at a repeat. In the decisive Game 5, won 80-75 by Detroit, Nolan played all 40 minutes and scored 24 points.

22. 2012 Indiana Fever

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-3

Defeated the Minnesota Lynx 3-1 in Finals

When Indiana lost its playoff opener 75-66 at home to Atlanta, there was no reason to think anything magical was in the works. Yet the Fever won the next two games and the series. The Fever also lost their opener in the East finals to Connecticut, but won 2-1 again.

Next up: A Lynx team that had the best record in the league that year. The Fever and Lynx split the first two games of the Finals. But in Game 3, the Lynx -- who led the league in offensive rating -- were held to a season-low 59 points.

Indiana had been up 2-1 in the 2009 Finals yet lost the series to Phoenix. But in 2012, franchise legend Tamika Catchings got her long-awaited title as the Fever won Game 4 at home.

23. 2007 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-2

Defeated the Detroit Shock 3-2 in Finals

Three years after winning her third title at UConn, Taurasi won her first WNBA championship. Phoenix's winning formula was coach Paul Westhead's run-and-gun offense, which was first in the league. Defense was not as much a priority; the Mercury were next-to-last in defensive rating. But it worked, with Taurasi, Taylor, Cappie Pondexter and Tangela Smith all averaging double digits in scoring.

The Finals matchup with defending champion Detroit got chippy, with Phoenix surviving a physical Game 4 in a 77-76 win. Then the Mercury became the first WNBA team to win a championship on the road, taking Game 5 108-92 at Detroit behind 30 points from Taylor -- who went 18 of 18 from the free throw line -- and 26 points and 10 assists from Finals MVP Pondexter.

24. 2004 Seattle Storm

Regular-season and playoff records: 20-14, 6-2

Defeated the Connecticut Sun 2-1 in Finals

This was Seattle's first trip to the WNBA Finals. And this was the last year that the Finals was a best-of-three series. The Storm were on the ropes after a 68-64 opening loss at Connecticut. But they pulled out a 67-65 nail-biter in Game 2 at Seattle, led by Betty Lennox's 27 points. In Game 3, with KeyArena packed with Storm fans wielding thunder sticks, Lennox had 23 points and earned Finals MVP honors as Seattle clinched the title 74-60.

25. 2015 Minnesota Lynx

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-3

Defeated the Indiana Fever 3-2 in Finals

Of the Lynx's four title teams, this was the only one with double-digit losses, as Augustus and Whalen both dealt with injuries. But big-time help came via two trades in July: first for guard Renee Montgomery and then for center Sylvia Fowles, who had sat out the season to that point to force a trade from Chicago.

Moore, the 2014 MVP, was again brilliant in 2015, leading the Lynx in scoring in the Regular-season (20.6 PPG) and the postseason (23.4). She hit a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to win Game 3 of the Finals vs. Indiana 80-77. The Fever won Game 4, but Fowles cemented her Finals MVP award with 20 points and 11 rebounds in a Game 5 victory.

26. 2009 Phoenix Mercury

Regular-season and playoff records: 23-11, 7-4

Defeated the Indiana Fever 3-2 in Finals

This was a good team led by a great player in Taurasi, who won her only regular-season MVP award in 2009. Like the 2007 champions, the Mercury focused on outscoring foes: Phoenix was first in offensive rating and last in defensive rating. Five players averaged in double figures, led by Taurasi's 20.4 PPG and Pondexter's 19.1.

The first game of the 2009 Finals was amazing: a 120-116 Mercury victory over Indiana. But the Fever took the next two games and had a chance to close out the series at home. Phoenix's defense showed up for Game 4, holding the Fever to a series-low 77 points. In Game 5, Taurasi and Pondexter combined for 50 points to win their last game as Phoenix teammates. Pondexter requested and got a trade to New York the next year.

27. 2021 Chicago Sky
Regular-season and playoff records: 16-16, 8-2

Defeated the Phoenix Mercury 3-1 in Finals

With longtime Sparks star Candace Parker coming to her hometown of Chicago as a free agent, there were big expectations for the 2021 Sky. Chicago went .500 in the Regular-season, the worst record of any championship team. But all the pieces were there -- including point guard Courtney Vandersloot and guard/forward Kahleah Copper -- to win a title.

The No. 6 seed, the Sky beat Dallas in the first round and Minnesota in the second. Then they went against No. 1 seed Connecticut in the semifinals. A double-overtime win in the first game of the series was pivotal, and Chicago won 3-1. In the Finals, the Sky won 3-1 over Phoenix, with Parker celebrating with family as the franchise won its first title.

28. 1997 Houston Comets

Regular-season and playoff records: 18-10, 2-0

Defeated the New York Liberty in championship game

This is where it all started, with the Comets winning the inaugural championship of the WNBA, which launched with eight teams. Cooper at age 34 was the best player in the new league, averaging 22.2 points and being named MVP. They played just single-game semifinals and finals in the first year, and Cooper scored 31 and 25 points in those victories. Thompson, who had been the top pick in the college draft, averaged 13.2 points and Brazil's Arcain 10.9. Swoopes gave birth to a son on June 25, just after the WNBA season had started. She played her first game on Aug. 7, and appeared in nine regular-season and two playoff games.

29. 2008 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 22-12, 7-2

Defeated the San Antonio Silver Stars 3-0 in Finals

By the time the Stars met the Shock in the WNBA Finals, Detroit was the better team. Five Shock players averaged in double figures in the Regular-season, led by Nolan and Smith. A late-season trade brought McWilliams-Franklin to Detroit, and she averaged 12.9 points and 7.8 rebounds in the playoffs. Smith won Finals MVP honors as the Shock won their third WNBA title in six years.

Unfortunately, the franchise was nearing its end in Detroit. The Shock played just one more season in the Motor City before moving to Tulsa in 2010.

30. 2003 Detroit Shock

Regular-season and playoff records: 25-9, 6-2

Defeated the Los Angeles Sparks 2-1 in Finals

The Shock went from worst in 2002 (9-23) to first in 2003, ending the Sparks' attempt to three-peat. Former Pistons player Bill Laimbeer took over as Shock coach during the 2002 season and totally changed the team's culture. He drafted Cheryl Ford at No. 3 in 2003; she averaged a double-double (10.8 PPG, 10.4 RPG) and was Rookie of the Year. Cash, who had been the No. 2 pick in 2002, led the Shock with 16.6 points in the Regular-season and 16.3 in the playoffs.

Detroit lost the Finals opener to Los Angeles, but survived Game 2, winning 62-61. In front of a huge crowd at The Palace at Auburn Hills, the Shock took the title in Game 3 in an 83-78 win, led by 27 points from Finals MVP Ruth Riley and Cash's near triple-double (13 points, 12 rebounds, 9 assists).

"I think our team really embodied the city of Detroit," Cash said.

stories.headline: São Paulo Grand Prix 2026: Race in Brazil start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 heads to Brazil for the São Paulo Grand Prix, a week after Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Brazil for the São Paulo Grand Prix, a week after Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion.

The Mercedes driver finished the Mexico City Grand Prix in third and made history by becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton behind in second.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 20th round.

- The families that built Kimi Antonelli, F1 world champion

- How Kimi Antonelli overcame George Russell, Ferrari to become F1's youngest champion

- Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

São Paulo Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Friday, November 6

Practice One: 3.30 p.m. - 4.30 p.m.

Practice Two: 7 p.m. - 8 p.m.

Saturday, November 7

Final Practice: 2.30 p.m. - 3.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 6 p.m. - 7 p.m.

Sunday, November 8

São Paulo Grand Prix: 5 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the São Paulo Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autódromo José Carlos Pace
Situated in a neighbourhood between two artificial lakes, Interlagos (which translates to "between lakes"), first opened as a race track in 1940. Formula 1 first raced at the circuit in 1972 as a non-championship race before becoming part of the calendar from 1973.

It dropped off the calendar in 1980 after its bumpy surface was considered dangerous, but F1 returned to a shortened and updated version of the circuit in 1990, which coincided with the rise of Ayrton Senna to global stardom. Senna's S at Turn 1 is one of the best overtaking spots on the track.

The circuit is one of the drivers and fans favourites. It's short, undulating nature, mixed with changing weather, often produces a blockbuster race.

São Paulo Grand Prix

Circuit: Autódromo José Carlos Pace; São Paulo, Brazil

Previous winners in São Paulo

2014: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2015: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2016: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2017: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2021: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2022: George Russell (Mercedes)

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2025: Lando Norris (McLaren)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1973

Laps: 71 laps of 4.3km

Lap record: 1:10.540, Valtteri Bottas (2018)

Most wins: Alain Prost with six at Interlagos & Jacarepagua (1982-1984-1985, 1987-1988, 1990) and Michael Schumacher has four at this circuit (1994-1995, 2000-2002). Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2016, 2018, 2021), Verstappen (2019, 2023, 2024), George Russell (2022) and Lando Norris (2025).

Most poles: Ayrton Senna with six (1986, 1988-1991, 1994). Previous pole sitters on the current grid are Fernando Alonso (2005), Hamilton (2012, 2016, 2018), Russell (2022), Verstappen (2019, 2023) and Norris (2024 and 2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the São Paulo Grand Prix is due to be cloudy during Friday's practice, with thundery showers forecast on Saturday with highs of 27°C. Sunday looks like it will be light showers, with temperatures dropping to 19°C.

What happened last time out?

Norris carried his winning momentum into Brazil and put his McLaren on pole position. The Brit then went on to take a dominant victory in Sunday's race.

He extended the lead in the drivers' championship to 24 points from teammate Piastri with three races of the season remaining.

Verstappen had a remarkable drive after struggling with the car in qualifying. For the race, the Red Bull driver started from the pit lane so the team could fit a new engine and change the car set-up, and ended up recovering to finish third.

Mercedes' Antonelli finished second, with his teammate Russell in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli clinched his maiden world title last time out, so the pressure will be off his shoulders now after getting the job done in Mexico City. He could also break a few more records including most wins in a maiden championship season.

Verstappen leapfrogged to second in the title standings and won the race last week to take his third victory this season, so could be a threat to Mercedes.

Hamilton sealed his first pole position last time out for Ferrari and looked more comfortable in the car. The seven-time world champion, who is an honorary citizen of Brazil, has always been one to watch at this track.

Despite the drivers' championship being wrapped up, the constructors' is all to play for. Mercedes are in mathematical contention to win it in Brazil and will be looking to maximise points from both Antonelli and Russell.

The team need to outscore Ferrari by three points or more.
